summary:
[  edit  ]
The OSC Out  DAT  is used for sending information over a OSC connection between remotely located computers. Use the   .sendOSC()   python method to output the OSC messages.
OSC bundles allows you to send a group of messages in a single command rather than as separate, individual messages. The OSC Out  DAT   sendOSC()  function will accept a list of messages and send as a bundle when you set the kwarg  asBundle=True .
Bundles were created as a performance optimization for real-time control of synthesizers with a large number of parameters. (thx Jesse Gilbert)
See also  OSC ,  OSC In DAT ,  OSC In CHOP ,  OSC Out CHOP ,  iOS and OSC ,  Network Protocols ,  Sync .
NOTE for Windows OS - If experiencing connection issues make sure Windows Firewall is disabled.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: While on, the  DAT  receives/sends information from/to the network port. While Off, no updating occurs. Data sent to the port is lost.

parameters.label: Protocol
parameters.name: protocol
parameters.description: ⊞  - Selects the network protocol to use. Refer to the  Network Protocols  article for more information.

parameters.label: Multi
parameters.description: Cast Messaging (UDP)   multicastmsging  -

parameters.label: Network Address
parameters.name: address
parameters.description: The network address of the target computer when using UDP. For multi-cast this is the multi-cast address to send to. This address is a standard WWW address, such as 'foo' or 'foo.bar.com'. You can put an IP address (e.g. 100.123.45.78). If you put "localhost", it means the other end of the pipe is on the same computer.

parameters.label: Port
parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The network port to send to.

parameters.label: Local Address
parameters.name: localaddress
parameters.description: Specify an IP address to send from, useful when the system has mulitple NICs (Network Interface Card) and you want to select which one to use.

parameters.label: Shared Connection
parameters.name: shared
parameters.description: Use the same connection as other networking DATs using the same network protocol.

parameters.label: OSC Address  Scope
parameters.name: addscope
parameters.description: To reduce which channels are generated, you can use channel name patterns to include or exclude channels. For example,  ^*accel*  will exclude accelerometer channels coming in from an iOS or iPhone app like mrmr. See  Pattern Matching  for the syntax of the possible channel name patterns.

parameters.label: Include Type  Tag
parameters.name: typetag
parameters.description: Includes the argument list type tag in each message. It includes the parameter type keywords (in case the parsing application needs to identify parmameter types).

parameters.label: Split Bundle into Messages
parameters.name: splitbundle
parameters.description: When On, each message contained within a bundle is given its own row.

parameters.label: Split Message into Columns
parameters.name: splitmessage
parameters.description: When On, OSC address and arguments are given individual columns, otherwise they are included in the message column.

parameters.label: Bundle Timestamp Column
parameters.name: bundletimestamp
parameters.description: When On, each bundle timestamp value is included in a column.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The Callbacks  DAT  will execute once for each message received.

parameters.label: Execute from
parameters.name: executeloc
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines the location the script is run from.

parameters.label: Current  Node
parameters.name: current
parameters.description: The script is executed from the current node location.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The script is executed from the location of the  DAT  specified in the  Callbacks  DAT   parameter.

parameters.label: Specified  Operator
parameters.name: op

parameters.label: From  Operator
parameters.name: fromop
parameters.description: The operator whose state change will trigger the  DAT  to execute its script when  Execute from  is set to  Specified  Operator  . This operator is also the path that the script will be executed from if the  Execute From  parameter is set to  Specified  Operator  .

parameters.label: Clamp Output
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: The  DAT  is limited to 100 messages by default but with Clamp Output, this can be set to anything including unlimited.

parameters.label: Maximum Lines
parameters.name: maxlines
parameters.description: Limits the number of messages, older messages are removed from the list first.

parameters.label: Clear Output
parameters.name: clear
parameters.description: Deletes all lines except the heading. To clear with a python script  op( "opname" ).par.clear.pulse()

parameters.label: Bytes Column
parameters.name: bytes
parameters.description: Outputs the raw bytes of the message in a separate column.
